tip: 'Tuh' points away from you: 'tuh lihat' = 'look at that over there'.
'Nonton' = spoken 'menonton' (watch): 'nonton film' = 'menonton film'.
'Ngobrol' = spoken 'to chat' (root 'obrol'): 'ngobrol' = 'mengobrol'.
'Duh' = 'ugh/oh no', the spoken groan for small disasters: 'duh, aku ketinggalan dompet!'
'Telat' = spoken 'terlambat' (late): 'telat bangun' = overslept.
'Titip' = 'get me…while you're at it': 'titip beli air' = grab me some water.
'Mendingan' is spoken 'better (to)': 'mendingan kita ke pantai' = better we hit the beach. Casual only – in writing you'd see 'lebih baik'.
'Minta ampun' after a quality = 'unbelievably': 'kotornya minta ampun'.
'Duluan' = spoken 'first/ahead': 'kamu duluan' = you go first.
'Bang' (from 'abang') = 'bro/mister' for young men: 'berapa sejam, bang?' Casual address.
'Main HP' = 'be on your phone' – 'HP' (ha-pe) is what everyone calls a phone in speech.
Doubling 'kapan' (when) blurs it: 'kapan-kapan' = 'sometime', no date attached. 'Kapan-kapan kita coba kafe baru' = we should try that new cafe sometime.
'Susah' = spoken 'sulit': 'susah fokus' = 'sulit fokus' (hard to focus).
'Gara-gara' means 'because of' with blame attached: 'gara-gara hujan deras', the rain gets the fault for the soaked shoes. Neutral cause is 'karena'.
'Surat keterangan' = an official note standing in for a document: 'surat keterangan hilang' = certificate of loss.
'Kartu keluarga' (KK) lists every household member – 'data di kartu keluarga juga harus diubah' = the family-card data must be changed too.
'Seumur hidup' = 'se-' (one) + 'umur' (age) + 'hidup' (life): 'one lifetime'. 'Berlaku seumur hidup' means the KTP never expires.
'Balik lagi besok' = come back again tomorrow – the classic counter phrase. 'Balik' = go back.
'RT' is the neighborhood unit; its head ('Pak RT') signs your 'surat pengantar' = cover letter for paperwork.
'Cap' = official stamp: 'dicap' = to get stamped. No 'cap', no service.
'Bolak-balik' = back and forth: 'disuruh bolak-balik' = told to go back and forth. Doubling here signals repetition.
'Beliau' is the respectful he/she for elders and officials: 'beliau sedang dinas luar'. Using 'dia' for a 'lurah' would sound too casual.
'Tinggal' + verb = all that's left is: 'tinggal menunggu' = just have to wait.
'Masa berlaku' = validity period: 'habis masa berlakunya' = has expired (lit. its validity is used up).
'Bikin' = everyday 'make, get made': 'bikin SIM' = get a license made. Casual but heard everywhere.
Documents 'die' in Indonesian: 'SIM saya mati' = my license has expired. 'Habis' works too.
'SIM keliling' = mobile license-renewal van ('keliling' = go around). Renew without the police station.
'Materai' = duty stamp stuck on official statements to make them binding. Sold at post offices.
'Dilegalisir' names a real ritual: getting official stamps on copies of your 'ijazah' so they count as true copies. Job and school applications often demand it.
'BPJS Kesehatan' is the national health insurance; nearly every resident is a member.
